title: Make one reversible decision with known unknowns

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A reversible experiment specifies an information question, bounded cost and stop condition. A consequential decision needs additional preparation: affected people, irreversible commitments, qualified input where needed and a decision date that does not outrun essential facts.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional study choice: Tue18:00–18:20 or Wed08:00–08:20. Both are free; usual evening noise may occur, morning transport begins 08:40. Study card: north is top, the desk is south of the hall, the shelf is east of the hall. Question: can the available setting support reading without displacing transport? Maximum cost 20 minutes; stop before required preparation.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Choose a trial and prediction, identify one missing fact and state the review decision before the outcome. Do not treat a trial as permission for a consequential commitment.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A trial subscription is reversible only before Friday, but its cancellation process is unconfirmed. Is “I can always undo it” a known fact?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Both windows can be defended with a stated uncertainty. Later fiction for morning:08:00–08:15 reading occurs,08:15 transport preparation starts unexpectedly early; session stops. This supports only 15 minutes of study and a revised preparation constraint. Partial: observe success but ignore changed timing. Incorrect: count 20 completed or generalize to all mornings. For a consequential course decision, separately gather fees, accessibility, withdrawal terms and affected commitments before agreeing; use appropriate advice for legal/financial questions.
criteria: Cost and stop condition are workable

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Verify the actual cancellation route and deadline before relying on reversibility; defer commitment if an essential condition is unknown. A reassuring assumption is not a stop mechanism.
criteria: Cost and stop condition are workable
